hints: Notice the two momentum arrows before collision: $4.0 \text{ N s}$ due east and $8.0 \text{ N s}$ directed up and to the left.
Recall that on a horizontal frictionless surface there is no external horizontal impulse, so total vector momentum is conserved when the balls stick together.
Add the vectors tip-to-tail: the eastward $4.0 \text{ N s}$ partly cancels the westward part of the $8.0 \text{ N s}$ vector, leaving a large northward part and only a small westward part.
walkthrough: Identify the initial vectors from the top view: $\vec{p}_1 = 4.0 \text{ N s}$ to the east and $\vec{p}_2 = 8.0 \text{ N s}$ toward the north-west.

State the physics: the surface is frictionless and horizontal, so net external horizontal force is zero and total momentum $\vec{p}_{total} = \vec{p}_1 + \vec{p}_2$ is conserved in the perfectly inelastic collision.
Resolve qualitatively: $\vec{p}_2$ has a north component and a west component, while $\vec{p}_1$ is purely east.
Combine components: north total is the full north part of $8.0 \text{ N s}$ and is large, west total is west part of $8.0 \text{ N s}$ minus $4.0 \text{ N s}$ east, so it is much smaller.
Conclude the resultant must point mainly north with a small tilt to the west, which matches the arrow shown. This is option B.

options.A: This points north-west with a large westward extent, but the $4.0 \text{ N s}$ eastward momentum cancels much of the westward part of the $8.0 \text{ N s}$ vector.
options.B: This shows a resultant pointing almost north with a small westward part, which matches the vector sum of $4.0 \text{ N s}$ east and $8.0 \text{ N s}$ north-west.
options.C: This points south-east, which is opposite in north-south sense to both initial momenta and cannot be the conserved vector sum.
options.D: This points almost south, but neither initial momentum has a southward component so the total cannot point south.
